appraisal_events.evidence: «répondit le duc avec une feinte humilité, mais avec une vanité si profonde que sa bouche ne pouvait s'empêcher de sourire et ses yeux de jeter à l'assistance des regards pétillants de joie sous l'ironie desquels rougit le pauvre historien»; the duc repeats his own opening clause «s'écoutant parler», flaunts «je ne suis que de l'Union et du Jockey», and presses «vous n'êtes pas du Jockey, monsieur ?» at a man who trembles without understanding the insult; he then recruits an ally with «Je suis sûr que vous êtes dans mon cas, Argencourt.»
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly unmasks the duc's mock-modesty as vanity and stages his club-name-dropping cruelty toward the defenceless historian, whom the narrator pointedly calls «le pauvre historien». The passage's own framing lowers the duc even as, inside the salon, his sally lands and silences its victim.

appraisal_events.evidence: «quand on s'appelle Saint-Loup, on ne s'amuse pas à prendre le contrepied des idées de tout le monde qui a plus d'esprit que Voltaire et même que mon neveu. Et surtout on ne se livre pas à ce que j'appellerai ces acrobaties de sensibilité, huit jours avant de se présenter au Cercle ! [...] c'est probablement sa petite grue qui lui aura monté le bourrichon. Elle lui aura persuadé qu'il se classerait parmi les « intellectuels ».»
appraisal_events.explanation: The duc publicly arraigns his absent nephew for betraying his name through Dreyfusism, mocks his intellect, ties his club candidacy to the scandal, and attributes his convictions to a kept woman's influence rather than to conviction. The narrator does not endorse the verdict — the same speaker has just been exposed as fatuous — but within the salon the condemnation goes unanswered.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's framing — feigned humility over deep vanity, the pleasure of listening to himself, the sport made of a helpless guest, the borrowed «ancien régime» phrases he only thinks are period — clearly lowers the duc within this passage.

Locally he dominates the table: his sally reduces his interlocutor to blushing and trembling, he enlists Argencourt as a witness, and his long verdict on Saint-Loup closes the passage unchallenged. The narrator devalues the man without denying him command of the floor.
Absent and undefended, Saint-Loup is declared unworthy of his name, less witty than everyone else, and a dupe of his mistress, with his imminent presentation at the Cercle cast as compromised.

ambiguities: The principal victim of the opening humiliation, «le pauvre historien» (l'historien de la Fronde), is an unnamed figure absent from the reference sheet, so the snub directed at him cannot be recorded against a listed character; it is folded into E1 as evidence of the duc's narrated diminishment rather than annotated as a separate event.

«sa petite grue», the woman credited with turning Saint-Loup into a Dreyfusard, is almost certainly Rachel, but she is not named in the passage and «petite grue» is not a reference-sheet surface form, so she is left out of characters_present; the discredit-by-association she carries is counted only through its effect on Saint-Loup in E2.
